subsystems.name: Robot units
subsystems.role: Small mobile robots that carry and place building material.

subsystems.name: Coordination algorithm
subsystems.role: Lets the swarm build without a central controller, using stigmergy.
parts: digital markers left in the environment

subsystems.name: Material system
subsystems.role: Building blocks designed to be handled by small robots.

subsystems.name: Localization and mapping
subsystems.role: Each robot needs to know its position and the state of the structure.

subsystems.name: Power and maintenance
subsystems.role: Keeps the swarm running for long construction tasks.

subsystems.name: Human interface
subsystems.role: Allows operators to set goals and monitor progress.

buildSteps.title: Define the construction task and blocks
buildSteps.detail: Choose a structure and design modular blocks that a small robot can lift (e.g., under 5 kg).

buildSteps.title: Design the robot
buildSteps.detail: Specify size, payload, locomotion (wheels for flat surfaces, legs for uneven), and sensors.

buildSteps.title: Develop the coordination algorithm
buildSteps.detail: Implement stigmergic rules where robots sense local progress and react, avoiding central control.

buildSteps.title: Simulate the swarm
buildSteps.detail: Test algorithms in software with physics to find failure modes and tune parameters.

buildSteps.title: Build and test a single robot
buildSteps.detail: Validate manipulation, movement, and battery life in a controlled lab environment.

buildSteps.title: Scale to a small swarm
buildSteps.detail: Run 10–50 robots building a simple wall or arch in a lab to observe emergent behaviour.

buildSteps.title: Demonstrate on a construction site
buildSteps.detail: Deploy to build a small structure like a shed or a wall, with human supervision.

buildSteps.title: Integrate safety and building codes
buildSteps.detail: Ensure the automated construction meets structural standards and can be inspected.

buildSteps.title: Scale up manufacturing
buildSteps.detail: Produce robots and blocks in volume for rapid deployment on larger sites.

prerequisites.why: Stigmergy and ant colony optimization are well studied, but robust construction in the real world is not yet solved.
Small electric motors and grippers are commercially available, but lifting capacity is limited.
Allows robots to share local state without a central hub.
GPS works outdoors but is not precise enough for millimetre placement; indoor systems need infrastructure.
Current batteries limit run time; swarms need frequent charging or battery swaps.
Most building materials are designed for human hands; interlocking blocks are being researched.

pathway.milestone: Lab demonstrations of small robot swarms building simple structures, such as walls or towers, in controlled environments.
pathway.unlocks: Proof that decentralized construction is possible.

pathway.milestone: Pilot projects on construction sites building small, non-critical structures like temporary shelters or landscaping walls.
Swarms building multi-story buildings or infrastructure with human oversight.
pathway.unlocks: Faster, cheaper construction for repetitive tasks.

pathway.milestone: Fully autonomous swarms building entire neighborhoods or cities.
pathway.unlocks: Rapid, large-scale urbanization, though regulation and economics remain hurdles.
